title: SEBI Master Circular for ICDR (Nov 11, 2024) — ASBA, UPI in public issues, and the T+3 listing timeline (Chapters 9, 10, 11)
publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
excerpts: Definition (verbatim, ICDR Reg 2(1)(d), reproduced in the Master Circular): "application supported by blocked amount (ASBA) means an application for subscribing to a public issue or rights issue, along with an authorisation to self-certified syndicate bank to block the application money in a bank account".

Applicability of ASBA (verbatim): "ASBA process is applicable in case of both Public Issue and Rights Issue. All investors (Retail, QIBs, NIIs etc.) / shareholders are eligible to apply through ASBA. All the investors / shareholders making application in public issue / rights issue shall use ASBA facility for making payment i.e. mention their bank account number and authorise the bank to make payment in case of allotment by signing the application."

UPI in public issues — introduction (verbatim, Chapter 10 para 1): "SEBI has introduced the use of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) as a payment mechanism with Application Supported by Block Amount (ASBA) for applications in public issues by retail individual investors through intermediaries (Syndicate members, Registered Stock Brokers, Registrar and Transfer agent and Depository Participants). This payment mechanism would increase efficiency, eliminate the need for manual intervention at various stages."

Key entities in the UPI-ASBA flow (verbatim, Chapter 10 para 2): NPCI — "National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), a Reserve Bank of India (RBI) initiative, is an umbrella organization for all retail payments in India." UPI — "UPI is an instant payment system developed by the NPCI... UPI allows instant transfer of money between any two persons' bank accounts using a payment address which uniquely identifies a person's bank a/c." Sponsor Bank — "Sponsor Bank means a Banker to the Issue registered with SEBI which is appointed by the Issuer to act as a conduit between the Stock Exchanges and NPCI in order to push the mandate collect requests and / or payment instructions of the retail investors into the UPI."

How UPI blocks funds (verbatim, Chapter 10 para 3.1): "For the purpose of public issues, UPI would allow facility to block the funds at the time of application." A retail individual investor applying through an intermediary uses his/her UPI ID for the purpose of blocking of funds; the investor approves a mandate, and the money is blocked (not debited) in the bank account until allotment.

Own-account rule (verbatim, Chapter 10 para 8.x): an investor "shall use only his/her own bank account or only his/her own bank account linked UPI ID to make an application... Applications made using a third party bank account or using a third party linked bank account UPI ID are liable for rejection."

T+3 listing timeline (verbatim, Chapter 11 paras 1-3): "it was decided to reduce the time taken for listing of specified securities after the closure of public issue to 3 working days (T+3 days) as against the present requirement of 6 working days (T+6 days); 'T' being issue closing date." The revised timelines for listing and the various activities are specified in Annexure XXIII. "The T+3 timeline for listing shall be appropriately disclosed in the Offer Documents of public issues." (Source circular: SEBI/HO/CFD/TPD1/CIR/P/2023/140 dated August 09, 2023.)

PAN and third-party verification (verbatim, Chapter 11 paras 5-6): before blocking ASBA application monies, the SCSB shall ensure "the PAN mentioned in the application matches with the PAN linked to the bank account of the applicant". The Registrar to an Issue undertakes third-party verification by matching the PAN in the demat account with the PAN in the bank account; "In instances of mismatch, such applications shall continue to be considered as invalid applications for finalising the basis of allotment."

Unblocking timelines (verbatim, Chapter 11 / para 13 cluster): failure to unblock funds in cases of non-allotment by T+2; failure to unblock in cases of partial allotment by the next working day from the finalization of basis of allotment (T+1). "The compensation to investors for delay in unblocking of ASBA application monies (if any) shall be computed from T+3 day."

Annexure XXIII — Indicative timeline of activities for listing of shares through Public Issues on T+3 day (T is Issue Closing Date), key steps verbatim/condensed:
• Issue Closure: T day — 4 pm for QIB and NII categories; 5 pm for Retail and other reserved categories. UPI mandate acceptance time: T day, 5 pm.
• Submission of final certificates: UPI from Sponsor Bank before 09:30 pm on T day; Bank ASBA from all SCSBs and Syndicate ASBA before 07:30 pm on T day.
• Third-party check (PAN): UPI applications completed before 9:30 AM on T+1 day; non-UPI applications before 1 pm on T+1 day.
• Finalization of rejections and completion of basis of allotment: before 6 pm on T+1 day.
• Approval of basis by Stock Exchange: before 9 pm on T+1 day.
• Fund transfer instructions (debit and unblock): initiation not later than 09:30 am on T+2 day; completion before 2 pm on T+2 day for fund transfer (debit); completion before 4 pm on T+2 day for unblocking.
• Corporate action for credit of shares to demat accounts: initiation before 2 pm on T+2 day; completion before 6 pm on T+2 day.
• Filing of listing application with Stock Exchanges and issuance of trading notice: before 7:30 pm on T+2 day.
• Allotment advertisement: on websites before 9 pm on T+2 day; in newspapers on T+3 day but not later than T+4 day.
• Trading starts: T+3 day.
notes: Source for the ASBA & UPI article and the listing-timeline article. Excerpts cover: the ASBA definition and universal applicability (all investor categories must use ASBA); the UPI-with-ASBA flow for retail (NPCI, UPI, sponsor bank roles; funds blocked not debited; own-account-only rule); and the T+3 listing timeline (reduced from T+6 in 2023), PAN third-party verification, and unblocking deadlines.
